title.en: It's time we did, I'd rather you didn't
title.es: Ya es hora de que actuemos

es: Reconocer It's (high) time e I'd rather + pasado en un debate familiar y distinguir crítica, preferencia y urgencia.

teaching.en: It's time we washed the dishes.
teaching.es: Ya es hora de que lavemos los platos.
teaching.explanationEs: It's time + sujeto + pasado: se habla de ahora; el pasado marca que ya toca actuar.
teaching.audioText: It's time we washed the dishes.

teaching.en: It's high time you helped with the chores.
teaching.es: Ya va siendo hora de que ayudes con las tareas de la casa.
teaching.explanationEs: High time suma un reproche: debías haberlo hecho antes.
teaching.audioText: It's high time you helped with the chores.

teaching.en: I'd rather you didn't use my laptop without asking.
teaching.es: Preferiría que no usaras mi portátil sin preguntar.
teaching.explanationEs: I'd rather + otra persona + pasado: lo que prefieres que haga alguien.
teaching.audioText: I'd rather you didn't use my laptop without asking.

teaching.en: I'd rather do the chores after dinner.
teaching.es: Preferiría hacer las tareas después de cenar.
teaching.explanationEs: Si el sujeto es el mismo: I'd rather + verbo base, sin to y sin pasado.
teaching.audioText: I'd rather do the chores after dinner.

teaching.en: I'd rather you didn't make so much noise at night.
teaching.es: Preferiría que no hicieras tanto ruido por la noche.
teaching.explanationEs: I'd rather you didn't + verbo es una forma cortés de pedir que algo pare.
teaching.audioText: I'd rather you didn't make so much noise at night.

teaching.en: I wish I lived in a quieter street; there is too much noise here.
teaching.es: Ojalá viviera en una calle más tranquila; aquí hay demasiado ruido.
teaching.explanationEs: Wish + pasado simple expresa un deseo sobre el presente.
segments: I wish I lived in a quieter
street; there is too much noise here.
teaching.audioText: I wish I lived in a quieter street; there is too much noise here.

prompt.es: Elige la frase que suena a reproche porque ya se ha tardado.

choices.text: It's high time we washed the dishes.
I'd rather we washed the dishes.
We washed the dishes yesterday.

feedback.es: High time añade reproche: los platos ya deberían estar lavados. I'd rather solo expresa preferencia y la tercera frase cuenta algo que ya pasó.

hint.es: Piensa cuál de las frases suena a «ya era hora».

prompt.es: Completa: «Ya es hora de que limpiemos la cocina.»

answer.text: cleaned

feedback.es: Tras It's time + we va el pasado simple (cleaned), aunque se hable de ahora.

hint.es: El verbo va en pasado simple, aunque el sentido sea de ahora.

origin.text: It's time we ___ the kitchen.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase dice Mia para pedir con educación que pare la música?

choices.text: I'd rather you didn't played loud music now.
I'd rather you didn't play loud music now.
I'd rather you to not play loud music now.

feedback.es: Con otra persona, I'd rather va seguido de didn't + verbo base. La segunda frase pone el verbo también en pasado y la tercera añade to.

hint.es: Con otra persona no se usa el presente después de rather.

origin.text: Mia's brother plays loud music at midnight. Mia wants him to stop.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Ya va siendo hora de que hables con ella.»

answer.text: It's high time you talked to her

feedback.es: High time + you + pasado (talked): reproche porque ya se tarda en hacerlo.

es: Expresar molestia con wish/if only + would, arrepentimiento con wish + had + participio y crítica con should have.

teaching.en: I wish my brother would stop borrowing my clothes.
teaching.es: Ojalá mi hermano dejara de tomar prestada mi ropa.
teaching.explanationEs: Wish + otra persona + would + verbo: molestia por algo que alguien hace y quieres que cambie.
teaching.audioText: I wish my brother would stop borrowing my clothes.

teaching.en: If only the neighbours would stop the annoying noise!
teaching.es: ¡Ojalá los vecinos pararan ese ruido tan molesto!
teaching.explanationEs: If only + would dice lo mismo que wish, pero con más emoción.
teaching.audioText: If only the neighbours would stop the annoying noise!

teaching.en: I wish I had studied more for the exam.
teaching.es: Ojalá hubiera estudiado más para el examen.
teaching.explanationEs: Wish + had + participio: lamentas algo que ya pasó.
teaching.audioText: I wish I had studied more for the exam.

teaching.en: You should have studied for the exam; it was important.
teaching.es: Deberías haber estudiado para el examen; era importante.
teaching.explanationEs: Should have + participio: crítica por algo que no se hizo.
teaching.audioText: You should have studied for the exam; it was important.

teaching.en: I regret shouting at her; I shouldn't have done that.
teaching.es: Me arrepiento de haberle gritado; no debería haberlo hecho.
teaching.explanationEs: Shouldn't have + participio: lamentas algo que sí hiciste.
teaching.audioText: I regret shouting at her; I shouldn't have done that.

teaching.en: I wish I had more free time.
teaching.es: Ojalá tuviera más tiempo libre.
teaching.explanationEs: Wish + pasado simple: deseo sobre el presente, no sobre el pasado.
teaching.audioText: I wish I had more free time.

prompt.es: Completa: «Ojalá mi hermano dejara de gritar.»

answer.text: would

feedback.es: Wish + otra persona + would + verbo: molestia por algo que hace alguien y quieres que cambie.

hint.es: Es una molestia por lo que hace otra persona.

I wish I had called her yesterday.
I wish I call her every day.

hint.es: Mira el tiempo verbal: el pasado va con had + participio.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Deberías haberme llamado antes.»

answer.text: You should have called me before

feedback.es: Should have + participio critica lo que no se hizo: aquí, no llamar a tiempo.

hint.es: Empieza por el sujeto y sigue con should have.

es: Comprender qué dilema plantea un texto y qué argumentos se dan a favor y en contra.

teaching.en: Leo's dilemma is whether to keep the wallet he found or return it.
teaching.es: El dilema de Leo es si quedarse con la cartera que encontró o devolverla.
teaching.explanationEs: The dilemma is whether + dos opciones: así se presenta el problema.
segments: Leo's dilemma is whether to keep the
wallet he found or return it.
teaching.audioText: Leo's dilemma is whether to keep the wallet he found or return it.

teaching.en: On the one hand, it is honest to return it; on the other hand, the money would help his family.
teaching.es: Por un lado, lo honesto es devolverla; por otro, el dinero ayudaría a su familia.
teaching.explanationEs: On the one hand… on the other hand… presenta dos argumentos opuestos.
segments: On the one hand, it is honest to return it;
on the other hand, the money would help his family.
teaching.audioText: On the one hand, it is honest to return it; on the other hand, the money would help his family.

teaching.en: One argument in favour of returning it is that the owner needs the money too.
teaching.es: Un argumento a favor de devolverla es que el dueño también necesita el dinero.
teaching.explanationEs: In favour of + -ing introduce una razón a favor; against introduce una razón en contra.
segments: One argument in favour of returning it is
that the owner needs the money too.
teaching.audioText: One argument in favour of returning it is that the owner needs the money too.

teaching.en: If he keeps it, the consequence could be that he feels bad for weeks.
teaching.es: Si se la queda, la consecuencia podría ser que se sienta mal durante semanas.
teaching.explanationEs: La consecuencia dice qué puede pasar después: If + presente, could / may.
segments: If he keeps it, the consequence could
be that he feels bad for weeks.
teaching.audioText: If he keeps it, the consequence could be that he feels bad for weeks.

teaching.en: Ana thinks her sister has a secret, but reading her messages would break her privacy.
teaching.es: Ana cree que su hermana tiene un secreto, pero leer sus mensajes rompería su intimidad.
teaching.explanationEs: Privacy es el derecho a que otros no lean lo tuyo; aquí es el argumento en contra.
segments: Ana thinks her sister has a secret, but
reading her messages would break her privacy.
teaching.audioText: Ana thinks her sister has a secret, but reading her messages would break her privacy.

teaching.en: Is it fair to buy a very cheap T-shirt when the workers who made it earn very little?
teaching.es: ¿Es justo comprar una camiseta muy barata cuando quienes la hicieron ganan muy poco?
teaching.explanationEs: Fair = justo: así se plantea el dilema de consumo.

prompt.es: Según el texto, ¿cuál es el dilema de Sara?

choices.text: Whether to accept the painting as a gift or pay for it.
Whether to keep the painting or give it back.
Whether to tell the truth or protect her friend's feelings.

feedback.es: Entre «on the one hand» y «on the other hand» aparece el conflicto: ser honesta o no herir a su amiga. Las otras opciones inventan un problema que el texto no plantea.

hint.es: Busca las expresiones on the one hand y on the other hand.

origin.text: Sara's friend shows her a painting and asks: «Do you like it?» Sara doesn't. On the one hand, it is important to be honest; on the other hand, she doesn't want to hurt her friend.

prompt.es: ¿Qué argumento se da en el texto en contra de leer el mensaje?

choices.text: His brother has the right to privacy.
The message is too long.
The phone belongs to Tom.

feedback.es: El texto dice «However, his brother has the right to privacy»: ese es el argumento en contra. Las otras opciones no aparecen.

hint.es: Busca la palabra However: marca el argumento contrario.

origin.text: Tom can see his brother's phone on the table. A message has just arrived, and Tom wants to read it. However, his brother has the right to privacy.

prompt.es: Completa: «Un argumento en contra de comprar camisetas baratas es que ganan poco.»

answer.text: against

feedback.es: Against introduce una razón en contra; in favour of introduciría una razón a favor.

hint.es: La razón habla de un problema: va en contra de comprar.

origin.text: One argument ___ buying cheap T-shirts is that the workers earn very little.

es: Defender una postura sobre un dilema con razones, un contraargumento y un arrepentimiento hipotético.

teaching.en: In my opinion, it is wrong to read other people's messages.
teaching.es: En mi opinión, está mal leer los mensajes de otras personas.
teaching.explanationEs: In my opinion + oración: presenta tu postura con claridad.
segments: In my opinion, it is wrong
teaching.audioText: In my opinion, it is wrong to read other people's messages.

teaching.en: There are two reasons: first, everyone has a right to privacy; second, trust is very important in a friendship.
teaching.es: Hay dos razones: primero, todos tienen derecho a la intimidad; segundo, la confianza es muy importante en una amistad.
teaching.explanationEs: First… second… ordenan tus razones para que se entiendan.
segments: There are two reasons: first, everyone has a right to
privacy; second, trust is very important in a friendship.
teaching.audioText: There are two reasons: first, everyone has a right to privacy; second, trust is very important in a friendship.

teaching.en: Some people say it is safer to check, but I disagree.
teaching.es: Algunas personas dicen que es más seguro comprobarlo, pero yo no estoy de acuerdo.
teaching.explanationEs: Some people say… but I disagree: presentas el contraargumento y lo respondes.
segments: Some people say it is safer
teaching.audioText: Some people say it is safer to check, but I disagree.

teaching.en: Although it may seem small, it can break a friend's trust.
teaching.es: Aunque parezca pequeño, puede romper la confianza de un amigo.
teaching.explanationEs: Although + oración completa, + idea contraria; no se añade but.
segments: Although it may seem small, it
teaching.audioText: Although it may seem small, it can break a friend's trust.

teaching.en: My opinion is simple: I would ask her instead of reading her messages.
teaching.es: Mi opinión es sencilla: yo le preguntaría en lugar de leer sus mensajes.
teaching.explanationEs: Instead of + verbo con -ing dice lo que harías en vez de otra cosa.
segments: My opinion is simple: I would ask
her instead of reading her messages.
teaching.audioText: My opinion is simple: I would ask her instead of reading her messages.

teaching.en: I wish I had asked her first; I broke her trust.
teaching.es: Ojalá le hubiera preguntado primero; rompí su confianza.
teaching.explanationEs: Wish + had + participio añade un arrepentimiento hipotético a tu argumento.
segments: I wish I had asked her
teaching.audioText: I wish I had asked her first; I broke her trust.

choices.text: Reading messages takes too long.
Her messages are probably boring.
People should be able to keep their things private.

feedback.es: La razón es el derecho a la intimidad (a right to privacy). No habla de tiempo ni de que los mensajes sean aburridos.

origin.audio: I think it's wrong to read her messages. First, everyone has a right to privacy.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase con su función en una opinión.

pairs: In my opinion, it is wrong to cheat.
First, it is unfair to other students.
Some people say it helps friends, but I disagree.
I wish I had studied more.

feedback.es: Una opinión bien construida combina postura, razón, respuesta al otro punto de vista y, si quieres, un arrepentimiento.

pairs: In my opinion, it is wrong to cheat.
First, it is unfair to other students.
Some people say it helps friends, but I disagree.
I wish I had studied more.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase responde mejor al contraargumento de Leo?

choices.text: Although many students do it, it is still wrong.
Many students do it, and that makes it right.
I agree, so I will copy too.

feedback.es: Although reconoce el argumento (muchos lo hacen) y lo rebate: sigue estando mal. Las otras dos aceptan lo que dice Leo.

origin.text: Leo says: «Copying homework is fine; all students do it.»

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué haría la persona en lugar de copiar.

choices.text: Copy only half of the homework.
Study together with the friend.
Ask the teacher for an easier exam.

feedback.es: Instead of copying introduce la alternativa: estudiar con su amigo. No propone copiar la mitad ni pedir un examen más fácil.

origin.audio: I would study with my friend instead of copying his homework.

prompt.es: Completa: «En mi opinión, es injusto para los demás.»

answer.text: opinion

feedback.es: In my opinion + oración es la forma de presentar tu postura.

origin.text: In my ___, it is unfair to the others.

prompt.es: Escribe tu opinión sobre copiar: postura, razones, contraargumento y arrepentimiento.

answer.text: In my opinion, it is wrong to cheat in an exam. There are two reasons: first, it is unfair to the other students; second, it breaks the teacher's trust. Some people say everyone does it, but I disagree. I wish I had studied more for my last exam.
accepted: In my opinion, it is wrong to cheat in an exam. There are two reasons: first, it is unfair to the other students; second, it breaks the teacher's trust. Some people say everyone does it, but I disagree. I wish I had studied more for my last exam.

I think cheating in an exam is wrong. First, it is unfair to the other students. Second, it breaks the teacher's trust. Some people say everyone does it, but I disagree. I wish I had studied more for my last exam.

In my opinion, cheating is wrong. The first reason is that it is unfair to the other students, and the second is that it breaks trust. Although some people say everyone does it, I disagree. I wish I had studied more for my last exam.

feedback.es: Una opinión completa une postura (In my opinion), dos razones (first, second), el contraargumento con su respuesta (Some people say…, but I disagree) y un arrepentimiento con I wish I had + participio.

origin.text: Datos: postura = está mal copiar en un examen; razones = es injusto para los demás estudiantes y rompe la confianza del profesor; contraargumento = algunos dicen que todos lo hacen; arrepentimiento = ojalá hubieras estudiado más para tu último examen.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase podría decir Ana ahora sobre su decisión?

choices.text: I wish I will ask her first.
I wish I ask her first.
I wish I had asked her first.

feedback.es: Ana lamenta algo que ya hizo: wish + had + participio. Will y el presente no se usan tras wish para el pasado.

origin.text: Ana read her friend's messages last week, and now they don't talk.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué hace la persona con el contraargumento.

choices.text: It answers the other view and says it is still wrong.
It agrees that it is only a small thing.
It changes the subject to another problem.

feedback.es: However marca la respuesta: aunque otros digan que es poco, sigue rompiendo la confianza. No coincide con el otro punto de vista.

origin.audio: Some people say it's only a small thing. However, it still breaks a friend's trust.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Aunque es pequeño, rompe la confianza.»

answer.text: Although it is small it breaks trust

feedback.es: Although + oración completa, y después la idea contraria sin but.

es: Discutir un caso escolar: exponer una postura, responder a la otra parte, expresar un arrepentimiento y acordar una decisión justa.

the money, because both ideas are good.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase reconoce el argumento del otro antes de responder?

choices.text: You are wrong, and that's all.
I see your point, but I'd rather buy books.
It doesn't matter what you think.

feedback.es: I see your point, but… muestra respeto por la otra idea y después responde. Las otras dos cierran la conversación.

hint.es: Busca la frase que reconoce la idea del otro antes de discrepar.

prompt.es: Completa: «Ya es hora de que hablemos con el consejo.»

answer.text: talked

feedback.es: Tras It's time + we va el pasado simple (talked), aunque se hable de ahora.

hint.es: El verbo va en pasado simple aunque el sentido sea de ahora.

origin.text: It's time we ___ to the council.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Lleguemos a un acuerdo y repartamos el dinero.»

answer.text: Let's compromise and share the money

feedback.es: Let's + verbo base propone una acción conjunta; compromise y share son las dos acciones del acuerdo.

hint.es: Empieza por Let's, que propone algo entre todos.

prompt.es: ¿Qué propuesta es un compromiso justo para Sara y Tom?

choices.text: Buy only the books.
Forget both ideas.
Use half for the trip and half for books.

feedback.es: Un compromiso da algo a cada parte: la mitad para el viaje y la mitad para libros. Las otras opciones dejan fuera a alguien.

origin.text: Sara wants to use the money for a class trip. Tom wants to buy new books. Both ideas are good, but the school has only a little money.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige de qué se arrepiente quien habla.

choices.text: That the decision was made without asking the students.
That the students decided without the teachers.
That nobody wanted to decide anything.

feedback.es: Wish we had asked lamenta no haber preguntado antes a los estudiantes. No habla de los profesores ni de que nadie quisiera decidir.

origin.audio: I wish we had asked the students before we decided.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase de la reunión con su paso.

pairs: In my opinion, the trip is more important.
I see your point, but the books are cheaper.
It's high time we voted.
Let's compromise and use half for each.

feedback.es: En una reunión primero se expone la postura, después se responde al otro, se urge a decidir y se cierra con un acuerdo.

answer.text: voted

feedback.es: I'd rather + we + pasado simple (voted) propone con cortesía lo que prefieres que haga el grupo.

origin.text: I'd rather we ___ first.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué reprocha la persona.

choices.text: The money was spent on books.
The money should have been shared earlier.
The vote was held too early.

feedback.es: Should have shared critica lo que no se hizo: repartir el dinero desde el principio. No dice que se gastara en libros.

origin.audio: We should have shared the money from the start. It wasn't fair.

prompt.es: Según el texto, ¿qué argumento da Mia a favor de comprar libros?

choices.text: The team has nothing to play with.
Books are cheaper than balls.
Books help more students.

feedback.es: Mia dice «books help more students»; la frase del equipo sin material es el argumento de Leo. El precio no se menciona.

origin.text: The council's dilemma: the money can buy books for the library or new balls for the sports team. Mia says books help more students. Leo says the team has nothing to play with.

prompt.es: Escribe tu intervención: postura y razón, respuesta al otro, arrepentimiento y acuerdo.

answer.text: In my opinion, we should share the money because it is fair to both groups. Leo, I see your point, but books help more students. I wish we had asked everyone earlier. Let's compromise because both ideas are good: half for books and half for sports. It's time we voted.
accepted: In my opinion, we should share the money because it is fair to both groups. Leo, I see your point, but books help more students. I wish we had asked everyone earlier. Let's compromise because both ideas are good: half for books and half for sports. It's time we voted.

I think we should share the money because it is fair to both groups. Leo, I see your point, but books help more students. I wish we had asked everyone earlier. Let's compromise: half for books and half for sports. It's high time we voted.

In my opinion, it is fair to share the money, so both groups are happy. I see your point, Leo, but books help more students. I wish we had asked the students before. Let's compromise and use half for books and half for sports, and then let's vote.

feedback.es: Un buen cierre une postura y razón (In my opinion… because…), respuesta al otro (I see your point, but…), arrepentimiento (I wish we had asked…) y acuerdo (Let's compromise).

origin.text: Datos: postura = repartir el dinero porque es justo para los dos grupos; Leo dice que el equipo no tiene material, pero tú crees que los libros ayudan a más estudiantes; te arrepientes de no haber preguntado a todos antes; propones un acuerdo: mitad para libros y mitad para deporte; ya es hora de votar.

prompt.es: ¿Qué lamenta Leo?

choices.text: That the decision was not made earlier.
That he voted for the wrong idea.
That the money is too little.

feedback.es: Wish we had decided earlier lamenta haber tardado; ahora casi no queda tiempo. No dice que votara mal ni que falte dinero.

origin.text: Leo says: «I wish we had decided earlier. Now there is almost no time left.»

prompt.es: Escucha y elige cómo responde la persona a la otra idea.

choices.text: It rejects the idea and ends the talk.
It accepts the idea and prefers books for a reason.
It agrees and changes to sports equipment.

feedback.es: Reconoce el argumento (I see your point) y mantiene su preferencia con una razón. No lo rechaza sin más ni cambia de postura.

origin.audio: I see your point, but I'd rather we bought books first, because more students can use them.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Ya va siendo hora de que tomemos una decisión.»

answer.text: It's high time we made a decision

feedback.es: High time + we + pasado simple (made): urge a decidir y añade un pequeño reproche.
